title: Require hosted Playwright success in the aggregate CI gate
description:
Validation enabler discovered while integrating panel acceptance criteria. The repository already has a separate `ui-playwright` job that installs the pinned pnpm 12.9.1 dependencies and browser and runs `pnpm run test:e2e`; however, the aggregate `test` job did not depend on that result. Phase 1 adds the dependency and fails closed unless the job succeeds. The protected main branch at base d4bc8e7 requires the aggregate `test` and `codeql`; `test` depends on `ui-playwright`, so browser validation is transitively required. This issue remains open until hosted same-head checks pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The aggregate `test` job depends on `ui-playwright` and fails if its result is failure, cancelled, or skipped while applicable.
- [x] The workflow contract asserts both the dependency and fail-closed result semantics. A future job condition must define applicability and cannot silently skip a relevant UI PR test.
- [ ] A hosted UI PR run passes Playwright and reports the result on the same head as the aggregate gate.
- [x] Verified branch protection at base d4bc8e7: protected `main` requires aggregate `test` and `codeql`; `test` requires `ui-playwright` transitively, not as a separate context.

## Test Plan
- Run the CI workflow contract and actionlint.
- Run `pnpm run test:e2e` locally when the environment permits the configured web-server bind.
- Verify hosted success and artifacts on a UI PR.
- Branch API confirmed required checks (`test`, `codeql`) on protected `main`; verify hosted same-head job results remain green.

## Scope
This is a CI validation enabler, not a finding from the UX panel. Do not change app product behavior in this issue.
acceptance_criteria: - The aggregate test job depends on ui-playwright and fails on a failed or skipped applicable result. - Workflow contract tests assert the dependency and fail-closed behavior. - Hosted Playwright passes on the same UI PR head as the aggregate gate. - Branch-protection required-check status is verified before claiming it is required.

- [ ] Contrast values and color token decisions are documented in a repeatable UI check.

Add a deterministic contrast-unit check for theme color tokens and a browser computed-style check for rendered contained/outlined buttons. Manually inspect hover/focus/disabled states. Run UI typecheck, Vitest, build, and Playwright. Target applies to the measured 4.2884:1 default pair.

title: Keep missing, empty, sample, and imported telemetry states distinct
description:
Finding: UX-01 from the 2026-10-05 frontend UX adversarial panel.
Source: Review report UX-01; ui/src/insight-engine.ts:146-153 and ui/src/App.tsx:190-213.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Load the preview. 2. Apply a payload with explicit empty arrays. 3. Observe whether sample seeds appear. 4. Apply blank input and compare the visible insights. 5. Use Reset to Sample.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Explicit empty arrays remain empty and render a deliberate empty state; they do not silently select seeds.
- [ ] Missing fields and explicit empty collections have defined, separately tested behavior. Imported empty-state copy does not label results as a sample window.
- [ ] Blank Apply does not silently replace current insights with sample data.
- [ ] Reset to Sample is the only action that loads sample records, and the result is visibly labeled as sample.
- [ ] Empty and partial imports do not receive sample recommendations or action-route instructions.
- [ ] A pulse score requires at least one commit-risk and one bottleneck record. Empty collections are no observations and display an unavailable score rather than 100/100; partial imports missing either input also display unavailable.
- [ ] Invalid input does not replace the last valid dashboard state.
- Imported empty-state copy does not describe data as a sample window.
- Risk records with no reason factors state that the reasons are unavailable without implying sample data.

## Test Plan
Add unit tests for missing, empty, and populated collections. Add component tests for blank Apply, explicit Reset to Sample, last-good-state preservation, and empty-import quality-pulse behavior. Add a Playwright flow for sample/imported/empty labels. Run pnpm exec tsc -b, pnpm exec vitest run, pnpm run build, and pnpm run test:e2e.

## Scope and delivery
This item applies only to the React/Vite browser preview unless the scope decision explicitly creates a separate item. Preserve native Rust shell contracts. Implement under parent milestone BI-5u3.1; collect evidence before marking complete.


## Phase 1 implementation snapshot — 2026-10-06
Implementation distinguishes omitted collections from explicit empty arrays and prevents imported partial payloads from receiving demo seeds. Missing, partial, complete-empty, and populated states have unit/component coverage; Empty and partial imports now suppress sample-only recommendations and hard-coded action-route instructions; the pulse score is unavailable unless both commit-risk and bottleneck records exist; empty arrays do not mean perfect quality. Unit/component coverage protects the empty state and real-data recommendations. Hosted same-head validation remains pending. Keep open pending hosted Playwright and aggregate checks. Local Playwright is blocked by sandbox `EPERM` on `127.0.0.1:4173`; see the dated Phase 1 validation note.
acceptance_criteria:
- Explicit empty arrays remain empty and render a deliberate empty state; they do not silently select seeds.
- Missing fields and explicit empty collections have defined, separately tested behavior.
- Blank Apply does not silently replace current insights with sample data.
- Reset to Sample is the only action that loads sample records, and the result is visibly labeled as sample.
- Invalid input does not replace the last valid dashboard state.
- Imported empty-state copy does not describe data as a sample window.
- Risk records with no reason factors state that the reasons are unavailable without implying sample data.

title: Validate responsive layout and priority task flow before changing layout
description:

title: Do not label absent bottlenecks as imported data
description:
Finding: PR #114 review comment “Hide the sample bottleneck for no-data imports.”

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Import an empty payload or a payload without stages.
2. Inspect the Quality Pulse Top bottleneck metric and Top Bottleneck explainability trace.
3. Confirm neither presents the sample fallback stage as imported telemetry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Empty/partial imports represent an absent top bottleneck as unavailable; they do not substitute the sample “review” label.
- [ ] The Quality Pulse metric and explainability trace both show an explicit unavailable state and identify that no bottleneck records are available.
- [ ] Sample mode retains its current sample fallback behavior.
- [ ] Existing imported bottleneck names remain unchanged.

## Test Plan
- Unit-test buildQualityPulse with empty and partial imported inputs and with sample fallback enabled.
- Unit-test explainability text for absent and present bottleneck inputs.
- Component-test the empty/partial import metric label.
- Add a Playwright assertion for the empty-import metric and explainability trace.
- Run TypeScript, Vitest, production build, Playwright discovery, and hosted same-head UI/aggregate checks.
acceptance_criteria: - Empty/partial imports show the top bottleneck as unavailable, never the sample “review” label. - Explainability states that no bottleneck records are available for imported input. - Sample mode and populated imported bottleneck names remain unchanged. - Unit/component/browser tests cover empty, partial, sample, and populated modes.

title: Represent absent imported top-risk data as unavailable
description:

## Steps to Reproduce

2. Inspect the Top Risk Commit explainability trace.
3. Confirm the trace does not display a blank identifier or present missing records as low risk.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Empty/partial imported data with no commit-risk records shows an explicit unavailable summary, not a blank identifier.
- [ ] The trace states that no commit-risk records are available and uses a neutral unavailable status, not a good/low-risk status.
- [ ] Sample mode and populated imported commit IDs retain their current behavior.

## Test Plan

- Unit-test explainability text and status for absent and present risk records.
- Component-test the empty-import trace.
- Add a Playwright assertion for the no-commit import trace.
- Run TypeScript, Vitest, production build, Playwright discovery, and hosted same-head UI/aggregate checks.
acceptance_criteria: - Empty/partial imports with no commit-risk records show Top Risk Commit as Unavailable, not a blank value. - Explainability says no commit-risk records are available and uses a neutral unavailable status. - Sample mode and populated imported commit IDs remain unchanged. - Unit/component/browser tests cover empty, partial, sample, and populated data.

title: Do not mark absent risk and stage trends as healthy
description:
Finding: PR #114 review comment “Distinguish absent telemetry from healthy trends.”

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Import an empty payload or a partial payload without commit or stage observations.
2. Inspect the PR Risk Trajectory and Bottleneck Pressure trend lines.
3. Confirm missing observations are not represented as green zero/healthy results.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Without commit-risk records, the PR Risk Trajectory value is Unavailable with neutral status and explicit no-record copy.
- [ ] Without bottleneck records, Bottleneck Pressure is Unavailable with neutral status and explicit no-record copy.
- [ ] When records exist and none are risky/pressured, the cards continue to show observed zero/healthy results.
- [ ] Sample-mode results remain unchanged.

## Test Plan
- Unit-test dashboard visuals for empty, partial, healthy populated, and high-risk/pressured data.
- Component-test empty and partial import trend values and visual status.
- Add a Playwright assertion for empty-import risk and bottleneck trends.
- Run TypeScript, Vitest, production build, Playwright discovery, and hosted same-head UI/aggregate checks.
acceptance_criteria: - No commit-risk records produce an Unavailable neutral PR Risk Trajectory, not a green zero/healthy result. - No bottleneck records produce an Unavailable neutral Bottleneck Pressure, not a green zero/healthy result. - Populated healthy records still show observed healthy zero counts. - Sample mode remains unchanged; unit/component/browser tests cover these states.

title: Derive populated import action routes from active telemetry
description:
PR #114 review follow-up: a complete populated imported payload currently has every stakeholder action route suppressed as Awaiting telemetry. Routes must be grounded in actual imported records without sample fallbacks.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Import a complete payload containing commits, stages, and signals.
2. Inspect Quality Pulse > Action Routing for each stakeholder.
3. Confirm populated imports do not show Awaiting telemetry when relevant records exist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Populated imported lead routes derive from commit IDs, levels, scores, and observed reasons.
- Manager routes derive from stage names/statuses and distinguish healthy observed stages.
- Executive routes derive from opportunity titles and scores.
- Security routes derive from imported dependency/automation signals or explicitly report none.
- Routes without relevant observations stay Awaiting telemetry and do not invent actions.
- Sample mode retains current routes.

## Test Plan
- Unit-test complete populated imports, absent/partial inputs, and sample mode for all audiences.
- Component-test populated route rendering for all audiences, no-data behavior, and absence of sample IDs/actions.
- Extend Playwright import coverage for populated commit, stage, opportunity, and security route data.
- Run pinned UI typecheck, Vitest, production build, Playwright discovery, and hosted same-head UI/aggregate checks.
acceptance_criteria: Populated imported lead routes derive from commit IDs, levels, scores, and observed reasons. Manager routes derive from stage names/statuses and distinguish healthy observed stages. Executive routes derive from opportunity titles and scores. Security routes derive from imported dependency/automation signals or explicitly report none. Routes without relevant observations stay Awaiting telemetry and do not invent actions. Sample mode retains current routes. Unit, component, and browser tests cover populated, absent/partial, and sample inputs for all audiences.
